- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.00 to -1.00 within 3 days), model overreacts; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85 multiplier) to forecast for 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use 5-day rolling average as anchor for correction.
